learningObjectives: Explain why a dated receipt, not a chat transcript, is the durable memory that lets a later session or agent avoid re-deriving state a prior one already established.

Distinguish a receipt (a dated record of what was found or done) from a transcript artifact (a log of how the conversation went) and from a living document (knowledge that gets revised in place, never appended-to).
Write a minimal receipt for a bounded piece of work: what was checked, what was found, what changed, and what remains open.
Identify when a reconciled multi-agent findings set is itself a receipt that must be written before a session ends, not re-derived by the next session from subagent history.
definitions: Receipt: a dated record of an outcome (what was found, decided, or built) that another session or agent can read instead of re-deriving the same state.
Lifecycle journal: the durable record of what agents were dispatched, on what task, so a later session can recover what happened without reconstructing it from memory or transcripts.
Living document: a carrier (a note, a guide) that is revised in place as understanding improves, as opposed to an append-only log.

Falsehood removal, never annotation: when a document is wrong, the correction replaces the false text outright — no 'Correction:' labels, no dated 'Verified' blocks, no provenance footnotes piling up around the true statement.
facilitationPlan: Live 90-minute session. Open with the operating problem receipts solve: a solo operator (or small team) running many agent sessions across days cannot hold every prior session's findings in their own head, and re-deriving them each time is expensive and error-prone. Show the shape of a real dated receipt (what fields it needs: date, what was checked, what was found, what changed, what's still open) without requiring any specific tooling. Run a live exercise: participants take a real piece of work they did this week (with or without agents) and write it as a receipt in under 10 minutes, then read one aloud for group feedback on whether a stranger reading only that receipt could pick up the work correctly. Close on the annotation-versus-correction distinction: a wrong receipt gets fixed by rewriting it true, not by appending a correction note on top of the false one.
humanFrame: Treat every session as if it will be read only through what it left behind, not through what its operator remembers. A receipt is a gift to your future self or teammate; a transcript is not a substitute for one.
assessment: Given a paragraph of raw session narrative ('the agent looked at three files, found two were fine, fixed the third, tests passed'), participants convert it into a minimal structured receipt and identify which sentence, if any, belongs in a transcript rather than the receipt.
